subject: Trial scoping — success metrics, owners & next steps (Peregrine POC)
content:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Megan Li <megan@peregrineanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Trial scoping — success metrics, owners & next steps (Peregrine POC)

Hi Megan — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our call and a proposed plan so we can get the POC scheduled next week.

Key goals we heard from your side:
- Validate accuracy/quality of model on your customer-facing triage flows (short form input)
- Achieve sub-100ms p50 latency for single-turn requests and p95 under 400ms for typical payloads
- Support sustained throughput of ~80 req/s for peak testing (burst to 150 req/s optional)
- Keep cost per token modeled below $0.002 during the POC window

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or edit):
1) Quality: average intent-accuracy >= 92% on a ~2k labeled sample set provided by Peregrine; no single category < 85%
2) Latency: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 400ms, measured at your observed input length distribution
3) Throughput: sustained 80 req/s for 10-minute run with <1% error rate; smoke at 150 req/s for 2 minutes
4) Cost: simulated cost per 1k tokens queries <= $2.00 (model/config to meet this target)
5) Operational: runbook for fallback and model-variant routing during the POC

Timeline (proposed):
- Today/Tomorrow: Confirm dataset and owners
- Week 1: Baseline test (redwood runs a smoke with sample workload)
- Week 2: Iteration (tuning batching/quantization)
- Week 3: Full load test + quality evaluation
- Week 4: Readout + decision

Ownership / Roles (initial):
- Peregrine: Megan (POC sponsor), Data: provision labeled sample set and success test cases
- Redwood: Stephanie (trial lead), Ben (infrastructure & bench runs), Karthik (performance tuning), Monica (customer success, onboarding)

Next steps I propose:
- Megan: confirm dataset drop (S3 link or secure transfer) and any network constraints by EOD Wed
- Ben: will draft measurement plan and instrumentation (latency histograms, token accounting) and share by EOD Wed
- Monica: coordinate kickoff call schedule and invite stakeholders
- Megan: confirm the acceptance criteria above or propose edits by Thu

Attached: peregrine-poc-scope-v0.1.pdf (scope stub)

Thanks — happy to hop back on a short call if you want to walk the criteria together.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Trial scoping — success metrics, owners & next steps (Peregrine POC)

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we'll provide a 2k labeled sample + a 10k unlabeled slice for throughput testing. We'll need guidance on redaction before transfer (PII concerns).
- Throughput: 80 req/s sustained sounds right but could we target 100 req/s as a stretch? Our production bursts can hit that.
- Cost: $0.002/token is in the ballpark; can you provide an estimate for our expected token sizes? Average request is ~120 tokens in and ~60 tokens out.
- Compliance: we need a summary of how data is stored/retained for the POC (SOC2/retention). Can someone from your security team confirm?

Happy to sign the scope once we get those details. Kickoff early next week works for us.

Best,
Megan Li
Director, Product Operations
Peregrine Analytics
megan@peregrineanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Trial scoping — success metrics, owners & next steps (Peregrine POC)

Megan — quick follow on from our infra perspective. Proposed measurement plan (high level):

1) Baseline smoke (Day 1): run 5k requests from your unlabeled slice at 10, 50, 100 token lengths; capture p50/p90/p95/p99, error rate, and token counts.
2) Cost modeling (Day 1-2): instrument per-request token totals and derive cost-per-1k-token with current model config. We'll put a small dashboard in the Redwood Console for this POC.
3) Throughput test (Day 5): ramp to sustained 80 req/s for 10 minutes, then a 2-minute 150 req/s burst. Track errors and tail latencies.
4) Quality evaluation (Day 6-7): run labeled set, compute category-level accuracy and surface confusion matrix.

Owners (detailed):
- Ben Carter: POC infra runs, measurement dashboards, post-mortem
- Karthik Iyer: batching/quantization profiles and latency tuning; will own p95 reductions
- Monica Patel: onboarding, data transfer coordination, stakeholder communications
- Stephanie Nguyen: POC champion and acceptance criteria sign-off

Notes on security/retention: we'll use a transient S3 bucket (redwood-managed ephemeral) with 30-day retention by default for POCs, optionally configurable. For SOC2 specifics I'll pull in our security engineer and summarize in a short doc.

Attached: measurement-plan.xlsx (instrumentation checklist)

I'll schedule the kickoff for Monday 09:00 PT if that works — will send calendar invite after Megan confirms dataset availability.

—Ben

- Token sizes: avg 120 in / 60 out — please use these for initial cost sims.
- Retention: 30-day ephemeral S3 is fine; please send the short SOC2 retention note.

Kickoff: Monday 09:00 PT confirmed. Megan, I'll approve the scope after the retention + cost estimate are in the doc.
